title: 赠孟浩然
author: 李白
intro: The most famous poet of the Tang writes a fan letter to an older poet he admires: Meng Haoran gave up office for pine trees, clouds, moonlit wine and flowers — and Li Bai can only bow to him from afar.
analysis: 孟浩然比李白大十二岁，是唐代著名的山水田园诗人，一生没有做官。李白非常敬佩他，写了这首诗。第一联直接表白：我爱孟先生，他潇洒的风度天下闻名。第二联概括孟浩然的一生：年轻时就放弃了官位和车马，老了还高卧在松林白云之间。“红颜”对“白首”，一生的选择两句话就写完了。第三联写他的生活：在月下喝酒常常喝醉，迷恋山花不去侍奉君王。“中圣”是一个有趣的说法：古人把清酒叫“圣人”，所以“中圣”就是喝醉了。最后一联说：他的品格像高山一样，我怎么能仰望得到呢？只能在这里向他清高的人品行礼致敬。全诗语言自然，感情真诚，可以看到两位大诗人的友谊。
analysisEn: Meng Haoran was twelve years older than Li Bai, a celebrated poet of landscapes and country life who never held office. Li Bai admired him enormously, and this poem says so outright. The first couplet is a plain declaration: I love Master Meng; the whole world knows his free, elegant spirit. The second sums up Meng’s life in two lines: with a youthful face he turned down official carriages and caps; with white hair he still lies at ease among pines and clouds. “Rosy face” against “white head” — a whole life’s choice, start to finish. The third couplet shows how he lives: often drunk under the moon, “struck by the sage”, and so in love with flowers that he will not serve the emperor. “Struck by the sage” is a joke: drinkers once nicknamed clear wine “the sage”, so being “struck” by it meant being drunk. The last couplet says Meng is like a high mountain — how could anyone hope to reach up to him? All Li Bai can do is bow from here to his pure character. The language is natural and the feeling sincere; it is a rare glimpse of one great poet looking up to another.
background: Li Bai (701–762) met Meng Haoran (689–740) in Xiangyang, Hubei, probably in the late 720s or the 730s, and the two became close friends. Li Bai also wrote the famous farewell “Seeing Meng Haoran off to Guangling at Yellow Crane Tower”.
pronunciation: 中圣 zhòng shèng（中：喝醉，像“中暑”的“中”）；轩冕 xuān miǎn；揖 yī；夫子 fū zǐ。机器朗读“中”易读成 zhōng，已在朗读用字中替换同音字。
version: 采用通行文本。异文：“徒此揖清芬”《全唐诗》作“徒此挹清芬”（挹：舀取，意为只能在此领受他的清香），网站用通行的“揖”（作揖致敬）。

lines.lit: his elegant spirit is heard of throughout the world.
lines.en: the whole world knows your free and graceful spirit.

lines.lit: With a rosy face he cast off carriage and cap;
lines.en: Young, you turned away from carriages and official caps;

lines.lit: with a white head he lies among pines and clouds.
lines.en: white-haired, you lie at ease among pines and clouds.

lines.lit: Drunk under the moon, he is often struck by the sage (wine);
lines.en: Under the moon, you are often happily drunk;

lines.lit: enchanted by flowers, he does not serve the ruler.
lines.en: lost in flowers, you will not wait on any king.

lines.lit: A high mountain — how can it be looked up to?
lines.en: You are a mountain too high for my eyes to reach;

lines.lit: Only from here do I bow to his pure fragrance.
lines.en: I can only bow from here to the clean fragrance of your name.

words.note: 古代第一人称，现代汉语说“我”。
对男子的尊称，如“孔夫子”。今天有时开玩笑说“老夫子”。
古义：风度潇洒、有才华。今天“风流”常指男女关系随便，意思变了。
这里指年轻时；今天多指美女。

words.en: official carriage and cap — high office
to lie among pines and clouds — to live as a recluse
to be “struck by the sage” — drunk
words.note: 古人把清酒叫“圣人”，“中圣”就是喝醉。中：遭受，读 zhòng，像“中暑”。
事：侍奉，古义。今天“事”多指事情。
古义：怎么、哪里。现代汉语说“怎么”。
现代汉语“仰望”“敬仰”“高山仰止”。
古代的礼节，现代汉语“作揖”。

imagery.name: 松
imagery.zh: 松树四季常青，代表孟浩然隐居山林、坚守高洁的人格。
imagery.en: Evergreen pines stand for Meng’s life as a recluse and his unbending integrity.

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 白云自由来去，象征他不受官场束缚的隐士生活。
imagery.en: Clouds drift as they please — the free life of a hermit, untouched by official duties.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月下饮酒，写出他悠闲风雅的生活情趣。
imagery.en: Drinking beneath the moon shows his relaxed, cultivated way of life.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 迷恋山花胜过侍奉君王，表现他热爱自然、看轻功名。
imagery.en: Loving flowers more than serving the emperor shows how he treasured nature and cared little for fame.
